With V0 = 2 eV and E = 0.5 eV, the exact transmission is

T = 1 / [1 + V0² sinh²(κa) / (4E(V0−E))] = 1 / [1 + (4/3) sinh²x], where x = κa.

The approximation is T_approx = 16(0.25)(0.75) e^(−2x) = 3e^(−2x).

The ratio simplifies to

T_approx/T = e^(−2x)(3 + 4 sinh²x) = 1 + e^(−2x) + e^(−4x).

This ratio is always above 1 and decreases monotonically with x, so the condition holds for the given width and every larger one once it first holds. Setting y = e^(−2x), the requirement is y + y² ≤ 0.10, which gives y = (−1 + √1.4)/2 = 0.091608.

Then 2x = −ln(0.091608) = 2.39024, so x = 1.19512.

The decay constant is κ = √(1.5/0.0380998) = √39.3695 = 6.2745 nm⁻¹.

The smallest width is a = x/κ = 1.19512 / 6.2745 ≈ 0.1905 nm.
